agentic.summary: Agent asked for sensitive authentication data (PIN) and disclosed a full password in the chat; verification, escalation, promises and conduct show no policy violations in the transcript excerpts.

findings.quote: Please send me your preferred PIN number
findings.explanation: The agent explicitly asks the customer to provide a PIN. The policy prohibits asking for passwords, PINs, or one-time codes; this is a major violation.
The agent again requests the customer's PIN. Repeated requests for secret authentication data violate the rule 'Never ask for... a PIN' (major).
The agent writes out the customer's new password in full. The policy states the agent must never ask for, repeat or write out a password — this is a major violation.

full.summary: Agent asked for and recorded a PIN and revealed a new password (violating personal data rules). The agent also generated a new password without completing the required verification for an account-sensitive action.

findings.quote: Please send me your preferred PIN number
findings.explanation: The agent explicitly asked the customer to provide a PIN. The policy forbids asking for a PIN, password, or one-time code.
The agent again requested the customer's PIN (sensitive credential). Asking for or collecting PINs is prohibited.
The agent wrote out and revealed a password value. The policy forbids asking for, repeating, or writing out passwords.

findings.quote: I can't recover the old password and I need to generate a new one
findings.explanation: The agent proceeded to generate a new password for the account. The transcript does not show a full verification using the required items (e.g., account ID and/or order ID where required) before performing this account-sensitive action; while an account was pulled earlier, the verification steps shown are incomplete or unclear.

rag.summary: Audit of 40-turn conversation based on provided excerpts. Found a major personal_data violation (agent wrote out a password in chat) and a major verification violation (an account-sensitive action was completed without evidence of required full verification). No other policy violations found in the excerpts.

findings.explanation: The agent wrote out a plaintext password in the conversation. The policy explicitly forbids asking for, repeating, or writing out passwords. This is a major violation of the personal and payment data rules.

A password change (agent set a new password at turn 37) is an account-sensitive action that requires full verification (full name, account ID and order ID). The transcript shows the agent provided only a username and there is no evidence the required full verification elements (email and order ID) were collected before changing the password. Completing this action without the mandated verification is a major violation.
